title: Enzymes in Digestion

blocks.name: Enzymes in digestion
blocks.definition:
Describe the functions of enzymes as follows:
(a) amylase breaks down starch to simple reducing sugars
(b) proteases break down protein to amino acids
(c) lipase breaks down fats and oils to fatty acids and glycerol
State where, in the digestive system, amylase, protease and lipase are secreted and where they act

blocks.md:
- **Amylases** are produced in the **mouth** and the **pancreas** (secreted into the **duodenum**)
- Amylases digest **starch into smaller sugars**

blocks.alt: Diagram showing the breakdown of a chain of a starch molecule into individual simple sugar molecules, illustrating enzymatic starch digestion
blocks.caption: The digestion of starch

blocks.md: - Proteases are a group of **enzymes that** [break down proteins into amino acids](https://www.savemyexams.com/igcse/biology/cie/23/revision-notes/7-human-nutrition/7-1-human-diet-and-digestion/7-1-11-digestion-of-protein/?_ai=internal-linking) in the stomach and small intestine (with the enzymes in the small intestine having been produced in the pancreas)

blocks.alt: Diagram showing protease enzymes breaking a protein molecule represented by a chain of amino acids joined together, into individual amino acid molecules.
blocks.caption: The digestion of proteins

blocks.md:
- **Lipase** enzymes are produced in the **pancreas** and secreted into the **duodenum**
- They digest **lipids into fatty acids and glycerol**

blocks.alt: Diagram showing lipase enzyme breaking a lipid molecule into its products: glycerol and three fatty acid molecules.
blocks.caption: The digestion of lipids
